scope: Future local-server performance candidate only. No production, benchmark input, active formal or frozen specification change is authorized by this draft. Finish and preserve the immutable 100-warmup/1000-event baseline before evaluating or implementing it. The existing 300 ms p95 target remains unchanged and no improvement is promised.
policy_assessment: The frozen validateDraft endpoint requires authenticated scoped access, exact baseRevision, current policy and complete independent worker validation. Its prose does not explicitly require a fresh SQL read on every advisory request, but the current DocumentQueries.validate implementation does perform scoped read and ownedIds bridge calls on every request. Authentication and workspace/document ownership must be checked before every validation. A previous successful read alone is not proof of current authorization. This is an explicit reviewed behavior/architecture extension, not an already approved optimization; in particular SQL/storage outage and permission-change behavior must be decided and tested before freeze.

key_and_payload.key: Server-derived immutable principal ID, logical-launch ID, workspace ID, document ID and explicit immutable historical revision, represented as exact bounded values. Never accept principal, launch or workspace from a request. Revision 0 is valid. Do not key by current head, display name, source hash alone, bearer token or candidate-supplied authority.
key_and_payload.entry: Only an immutable defensive copy of the exact authorized historical artifact bytes and a bounded server-derived definition-ID-to-kind index for that same accepted artifact. Extract definitions from accepted module declarations, parameters, binders and owned expression definitions only; never infer ownership from arbitrary references, user strings or a candidate. TEXT_ONLY yields an empty local definition index. Cache has no response envelope, headRevision, mutable document state, policy decision, receipt, analysis/evidence, checked candidate or advisory result.
key_and_payload.bounds: At most 8 entries and at most 8 MiB accounted retained storage per process. Treat 8 MiB serialized artifact-plus-index bytes as a payload ceiling, not as a bound on JVM heap. Separately account keys, array/object metadata and a conservative fixed/per-entry allocation reserve inside the 8 MiB retained-accounting budget; atomically enforce entry count and accounted retained bytes before insertion. If overhead cannot be bounded, do not cache it. Transient copies, decoded JSON and worker frames remain under existing request/response/worker and aggregate-memory limits; a measured JVM heap profile is additional evidence, not implied by serialized byte length. Eviction is performance-only; oversize or cache failure falls back to existing scoped SQL.
key_and_payload.instance_identity: A singleton cache is allowed only when it captures one server-private immutable principal/workspace/logical-launch identity at initialization and compares each request-derived private scope to that bound identity before any lookup. A trusted non-secret metadata fingerprint or opaque in-process identity may identify that binding; worker build/dependency hash is not a workspace identity. Missing, corrupt, changed, or mismatched metadata disables/clears the cache and fails closed or uses the independently authorized SQL path; never expose the private identifier or accept it from a browser.

admission_and_lifetime.populate: Only after a successful, authorized, scoped SQL-backed store read of an actual retained artifact. Verify returned documentId and concrete requestedRevision exactly equal the trusted request's document and explicit revision before insertion; reject missing, duplicate, malformed or mismatched response fields. A GET without requested revision may warm only the concrete returned requestedRevision after SQL reads the head; never retain or replay the returned headRevision. Require successful complete response decoding and exact bounded artifact bytes before the immutable copy. Do not insert from a draft, worker result, commit request, client value, failed read, private-protocol parse error or speculative write.
admission_and_lifetime.integrity: Cache hit requires exact all-component key equality, defensive bytes and immutable definition index, and an authorized entry previously read for that exact scope/document/revision. Object aliasing, concurrent mutation, key collision or incomplete read cannot replace content. Recheck requested key and result content identity on insertion. No comparison relies on a hash instead of exact key equality.
admission_and_lifetime.lifecycle: In-memory only for one server-process incarnation bound to one private durable principal/workspace/logical-launch identity captured from trusted metadata, with an exact scope check for each request. Start empty; clear on shutdown/restart, workspace/principal/logical-launch rebinding, missing/corrupt/changed private metadata, store identity change, restore/recovery, document authorization change, or any invalidation event capable of changing a previously read key. A database restore, reinitialization or out-of-band mutation must be quiesced through process restart or an explicit synchronized invalidation barrier before serving further cache hits. Until that invariant is enforced and independently tested, disable the cache and use SQL. This cache does not change indefinite receipt/history retention or authorize public read/delete semantics.

preview_only.entry_checks: On every validate request run the existing bounded decoding, authentication, current authorization for this exact document, runtime readiness, current dependency/policy check and worker-permit acquisition. The current policy and worker identity are read from current authoritative runtime state each time, never cached. A cache entry or historical read is not a credential or a current authorization check. If current document authorization cannot be established independently and soundly under the immutable-ownership/lifecycle invariant, perform the scoped SQL authorization/read before using the cache; a hit alone MUST NOT satisfy the check.
preview_only.base: Only an exact revision-key hit may supply the immutable base bytes for advisory validation. A miss, invalid entry, changed scope or cache failure uses the existing SQL read; lack of required current authorization, policy, worker, database availability where mandated, or trustworthy cache state fails closed. Define the reviewed outage policy explicitly before implementation: this draft does not authorize serving cached validation during SQL/authorization failure.
preview_only.id_inventory: For each distinct candidate-referenced server ID, a cached accepted base definition supplies only that exact ID's recorded kind. Any requested ID absent from that base must still be resolved by the existing scoped ownedIds SQL lookup over authorized immutable document history. Wrong kind, missing or foreign IDs still reject. Locally derived hits and SQL-returned misses are merged without changing kind or granting extra IDs; no absent ID is considered fresh merely because it is absent from the cached revision. If a cached extraction is incomplete or ambiguous, bypass the optimization. All actual SQL, including misses, still traverses the required SQLeanParser proxy.
preview_only.worker: Always run the same complete isolated Alloy/parser/document worker on the exact current candidate, under current policy and dependency identity. Cache never stores or reuses a validation result or worker decision, and never changes draft/request hash or response freshness. Candidate draft IDs are not inserted into cache. Acceptance/denial of a preview remains advisory only and grants no later mutation authority.
preview_only.excluded_paths: Mutations, history-copy, admission, quota, receipt replay, final CAS, policy fencing, analysis/evidence and public GET/list results remain on their existing authoritative paths. GET may warm the cache only after returning from a successful scoped SQL read. No cache result establishes head revision, store transaction success, receipt existence, current analysis identity or canonical CorpusPair authority. Browser accepted state and source stay unchanged.

model.claims: An entry can be admitted only from an exact-key modeled successful read; while every cached key remains bound to the same immutable modeled store snapshot, a hit equals that exact snapshot and cannot match a different principal/launch/workspace/document/revision. Cache transitions preserve capacity and exact-store provenance. Existing stored definition lookup returns only a definition actually present in that exact snapshot. Advisory steps require supplied current auth/readiness/permit, call a worker with the current policy and candidate, and cannot change head/history/receipts. Revisions newly appended without replacing old keys preserve the provenance invariant.
model.explicit_trust: Lean treats Store as an abstract immutable function, auth/readiness/permit as external current facts, worker as a parameter, and Snapshot definitions as trustworthy projection of accepted source. It does not prove DB isolation or immutability, owner authorization, JSON parser, definition extraction, Java thread safety, defensive copying, byte accounting/heap use, runtime-policy atomicity, Java/TypeScript/SQL refinement, physical backup/restore safety or benchmark performance. These are separate checked adapters and/or integration tests. Admission before use and coordinated restore invalidation are preconditions, not conclusions of the model.

required_preimplementation_evidence: Finish the frozen baseline benchmark and report observed p50/p95/p99, sample count, warmup/cold phases and source fingerprints, including failures; do not conflate this proposal with the baseline result.

Freeze this candidate, exact prior 267 model registries and new exact propositions, registered verifier and baseline; obtain two Terra, two Sol and two Astra independent approvals followed by two isolated clean Lean builds before any cache implementation.

Show a current-authorization mechanism for exact document scope, immutable retained revisions and restoration/rebinding invalidation without relying on cache membership; review explicitly whether a DB outage should block previews. If no independent current check preserves policy, retain SQL on each preview.

Exercise miss/hit, cross-principal/launch/workspace/document/revision denial, ID kind/subset/history fallback, mismatched DB response, source-versus-block mode, malformed/foreign IDs, one-process restart, restore/invalidation and concurrent eviction/insertion. Check exact bytes, not only hashes, and prove no cache path can mutate accepted state, receipts, CAS or evidence.

Measure bounded retained and transient heap under worst-case 8-entry/8-MiB workload, enforce size/eviction under concurrent reads, and verify worker always runs with current policy/dependency. Test SQL proxy/bridge failures and ensure no direct-Postgres fallback.

Rerun the same frozen 500-node/1000-edit performance workload after reviewed implementation, compare distributions and preserve both raw evidence sets. Leave original 300 ms target and all inherited G2/G3 requirements open unless measured evidence satisfies them.
approval: DRAFT only: no release, runtime, benchmark success, implementation, production or commercial authorization.
